To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the sugar-perylene units are more efficient than the perylene units at stabilizing the duplex and triplex structures; 2) the perylene unit is more efficient than the sugar-perylene at increasing the fluorescent signal; 3) the perylenes coupled to the terminal phosphate groups are more efficient than those attached to the 2'-deoxribose residue.

ODNs involving a sugar-perylene unit attached to the 2'-position of a 2-deoxyribose residue are more efficient at forming triplexes and duplexes than those involving perylenes directly attached to the 5'- (or 3'-) phosphate group, and that the introduction of two perylenyl moieties at both termini of the ODN is the most efficient way to stabilize these structures.
the introduction of perylene units into ODNs at the anomeric position induces the formation of anomers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new DNA probes involving perylenes.
the design of new ODN-perylene probes for the detection of nucleic acids by means of the fluorescence technique.
the synthesis of ODN-perylene hybrids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ODNs containing two sugar-perylene conjugates attached at both terminus are the most efficient at stabilising the triplex and at increasing the intensity of the fluorescence signal.

the sugar-perylene conjugates are more effective than the ODN-perylenes conjugates involving the polymethylene chain at both stabilizing the tri- and the duplex structures and at increasing the fluorescent signal upon binding with the targets.

the introduction of two sugar-perylene conjugates attached either at both the termini or at the 5'-terminus and an internal position of an ODN chain is the most effective way of improving the stability of the triplex and of the duplex structures and of increasing the intensity of the fluorescence signal upon hybridization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hybridization properties of ODNs involving perylene conjugates are strongly influenced by the conjugation parameters.
the introduction of a single sugar-perylene unit into the ODN chain is inefficient at stabilizing the duplex and the triplex structures.

the introduction of a perylene moiety at the 5'-terminal phosphate group of a 2-ODN induces a destabilization of the triplex structure, whereas the introduction of a sugar-perylene moiety at the same position induces a stabilization of the triplex and of the duplex structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conjugation parameters of the perylene moiety have a great influence on the stability and fluorescence properties of the conjugate.

the introduction of two perylenyl units at either termini of the ODN is the best way to stabilize the triplex or duplex structures and that the use of sugar-perylene units is the most effective way to achieve this goal.
